answers.answer: Only the employee's direct manager (the `manager` of the employee who made the expense) can approve or reject it. Anybody else as `by`, including the employee themselves, is a Conflict on param `by`. An employee with no manager cannot submit expenses at all: submitting is a Conflict on param `expense`. Approving or rejecting an expense that is not `submitted` (a draft, or one already approved or rejected) is a Conflict on param `expense`.

An expense of 500.00 or more (50000 cents or more) needs two approvals: first the employee's direct manager, then that manager's own manager. Whoever is not next in that order, as `by` (approving and rejecting alike), is a Conflict on param `by` (so the skip-level cannot go first and the manager cannot approve twice). After the first approval the expense stays `submitted`; after the second it is `approved`. If the manager has no manager, the manager's approval alone is enough, and so it is for expenses under 50000. Rejecting works for whoever's turn it is and rejects the expense outright. The expense view shows `approvals`: the ids of the approvers so far, in order (an empty list before the first).

An expense can be submitted up to 30 days after its `date`, counted in calendar days (UTC) from the expense date to the day of submitting: day 30 is fine, day 31 is a Conflict on param `expense`. A date in the future is fine. It is checked only when submitting.

Submitting is only for drafts, so a rejected expense is final: the employee creates a new expense instead (submitting a non-draft is a Conflict on param `expense`). A draft is also refused as a duplicate (Conflict on param `expense`) when the same employee already has a `submitted` or `approved` expense with the same amount and the same date; draft and rejected ones don't count.
`expense.reject` also takes `reason`, a non-empty string (anything else is an InvalidRequest on param `reason`). The expense view shows it as `reason`, null until the expense is rejected.
